trap-thesis-restatement.notes: STANDING-TRAP FINDINGS, report only, do not fix inline. (1) The clause-(2) argument is not a proof: 'Under continuity, every limit point of {q : P(q)} is bar-conjugate to a limit point of not-P, forcing the symmetric extension.' P is Prop-valued, so 'continuous' can only mean locally constant, and on the connected R_{>0} that makes P constant - the conclusion is then vacuous rather than derived. The counterexample in the same clause is correct and does the real work; only the continuity half is unsupported. (2) The counterexample is described as 'bar-invariant on (a, a^{-1}) but false outside'; the indicator of a bar-symmetric interval is bar-invariant on ALL of R_{>0}, which is what makes it a valid instance of the hypothesis - as written it reads as if the hypothesis were only locally satisfied. (3) The worked application transfers 'q_0 > 1/phi^2 => E_{q_0} non-degenerate' to 'q_0 < phi^2 => E_{1/q_0} non-degenerate'. Clause (1) literally outputs E_{q_0}, not E_{1/q_0}; the two agree by bar-invariance, but the displayed step is not the clause being applied. (4) Band checked: phi^2 = 2.618033988750, 1/phi^2 = 0.381966011250, and q_0 = 1.1099785827513808 lies in the super-classical wing (1, phi^2) as the text says. Section 7a generator convention respected (sigma_i, never T). (5) Two trailing spaces at line ends in the clause block.
